source.title: Separability Is Not Alignability: Representations for Spectrum-to-Molecule Retrieval
source.authors: Karol Musielinski; F. C. Teh; Takahiko Koyama; Artur Dubrawski

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly measures spectrum–molecule representational agreement and frozen retrieval, and reports that stronger molecular separability does not ensure better alignment or retrieval. It also reports low cross-modal agreement and differing results across similarity metrics.
record.gate_note: The paper measures cross-modal geometry and tests adapters between frozen spectrum and molecule encoders. Results cited from other papers, including scale trends and other alignment studies, are not recorded as rows. Within-modality separability results are omitted because they do not themselves measure alignment. Retrieval and representation-alignment results from the paper's own experiments are included.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-modal agreement (mutual-kNN, linear CKA) between independently trained spectrum and molecule encoders on MassSpecGym, and evaluates frozen adapter retrieval. It argues that the Platonic premise of shared geometry breaks down for MS/MS: agreement is low and separability does not yield metric compatibility. It does not vary scale and uses no vision–language models.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that molecular separability does not determine between-molecule geometry. MS-JEPA clusters best yet retrieves worst when frozen, and cross-modal agreement stays low, which limits the frozen-alignment premise borrowed from the Platonic hypothesis. They add that candidate-trained adapters exploit a spectrum-blind decoy prior. They also find that simulated paired data, not frozen geometry, gives the largest gains.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates cross-modal geometry with mutual-kNN and linear CKA and tests frozen adapter retrieval; it does not reproduce a model-scale convergence sweep or the original study's scaling comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured cross-modal ordering differs between mutual-kNN and linear CKA. The paper also reports that spectral cosine–molecular Tanimoto correlations vary with pair-sampling protocol, but that is not a direct test of convergence between model representations.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding VA-VAE alignment loss toward MoLFormer geometry raises MS-JEPA mutual-kNN (0.029→0.064) and frozen MRR (0.105→0.192). For DreaMS it changes retrieval negligibly (0.227→0.230).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicitly supervising cross-modal geometry during unimodal pretraining increases alignment and frozen alignability, depending on the encoder.

fits_no_version.finding: Separability (silhouette 0.49 for MS-JEPA) is inversely related to cross-modal agreement and frozen retrieval across the encoders.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-modality clustering by identity does not imply cross-modal metric compatibility.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Representations for the Physical Sciences Workshop (review status not stated)
record.problems: The experiments are on one molecular retrieval benchmark and do not vary model scale or capability. Cross-modal geometry is measured using a limited set of encoders and metrics. The methods section states that models use one training seed except for JESTR repeats; bootstrap intervals capture test-sample uncertainty, not training variance.
record.rows_left_out: Within-modality separability, extended cosine–Tanimoto sampling results, and retrieval baselines not directly measuring cross-modal representation alignment were omitted. The study also reports cited results in related work; these are not its own results.

untested.parts: No sweep over scale, capability or compute.
No vision–language models or image–caption pairs.
No seed comparisons; each model uses one seed.
No linear maps, layer stitching, relative representations or unpaired alignment. Adapters are MLPs trained on paired data.
No sweep over k or input set; no out-of-distribution test of model–model agreement.
No test of a plateau with scale, and no test of shared data or objectives as the cause of agreement.

missing.what: End-to-end MRR versus frozen MRR for each encoder (DreaMS 0.244–0.255; MS-JEPA (A) 0.243; [CLS]/(B) 0.257; fresh encoder 0.232). Needed to judge how much the frozen map loses.
Individual mutual-kNN and CKA values for all pairs, including fingerprint, SMI-TED and MiniMol (e.g. ChemBERTa–SMI-TED CKA 0.535 versus mutual-kNN 0.113).
Within-modality molecule–molecule mutual-kNN references (0.11–0.29) as separate rows.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 label wrongly included r28; it is removed. V4 links were removed from mutual-kNN and CKA rows, because they measure kernel agreement rather than a map. The alignment-loss interventions are induced on purpose and are kept only for the metric-divergence contrast under V6 (r27, r29). Each model uses a single seed. The authors caution that mutual-kNN magnitudes depend on sample size, citing Koepke et al.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size, compute, or capability, and no test of whether alignment rises with scale.
No vision–language models or paired images and captions.
No comparison across random initializations of the same architecture, or test of shared features or subspaces across seeds.
Tests frozen spectrum-to-molecule adapters on this retrieval task, but not linear maps specifically, layer stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired training data.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are analyzed.
Tests mutual-kNN and linear CKA on one benchmark; does not systematically sweep metric settings such as k, or evaluate out-of-distribution inputs.
Shows low or incomplete cross-modal agreement, but does not test for a scale-related plateau or establish that shared training data or objectives cause the measured agreement.
